query: For high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation? Specify what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, the expected observations relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in high-entropy-alloy (HEA) multilayer coatings is governed by coherency-stress–driven back-stress hardening at A/B compositional interfaces, which impedes dislocation climb and glide during creep, thereby reducing steady-state creep rates relative to monolithic HEA coatings of the same average composition.
generation.material_initial_state: HEA multilayer coating with alternating coherent layers A and B (layer thickness 20–100 nm) and a monolithic HEA coating of equivalent overall composition and thickness.
generation.intervention: Apply constant uniaxial creep stress at elevated temperature to both multilayer and monolithic samples.
generation.conditions: Temperature 0.4–0.7 Tm; applied stress 0.2–0.8 GPa; layer thickness 20–100 nm; coherent (unannealed) A/B interfaces.
generation.structural_mediator: Coherency stresses at A/B layer interfaces generating back-stress hardening.
generation.mechanism: Under load, dislocations accumulate at coherent interfaces; the resulting coherency stresses oppose further dislocation climb/glide, raising the effective activation energy for creep and lowering the steady-state creep rate.
generation.predicted_outcome: Multilayer HEA coatings will exhibit 20–60% lower steady-state creep rates and an increased stress exponent compared to monolithic HEA under the same conditions.
generation.baseline: Monolithic HEA coating of identical average composition and thickness.
generation.boundary: Valid for coherent multilayers with layer thickness between 20 nm and 100 nm, temperatures 0.4–0.7 Tm, and stresses 0.2–0.8 GPa. Beyond these ranges, other mechanisms (e.g., diffusional creep) may dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Approximate magnitude of creep-rate reduction (20–60%) and precise increase in activation energy remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: 1) Fabricate: a) HEA multilayer coatings (A/B, 20–100 nm layers, coherent). b) Identical monolithic HEA coatings. c) Annealed multilayer coatings to relieve interface coherency stresses. 2) Perform constant-stress creep tests at 0.6 Tm and 0.5 GPa for ≥100 h on all three sample sets.
measurements: Apparent activation energy from T-varied tests
Residual coherency stress by X-ray diffraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If multilayer coatings do not exhibit at least a 20% reduction in steady-state creep rate compared to both monolithic and annealed multilayer samples under identical conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
